chapter: The 1920s road: dance style and management
title: The Cleveland boy he hired as a valet
summary: He told a 13- or 14-year-old he met in Cleveland to come to New York at 15, and gave him a job running errands.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: But I didn't want to get married to prove that to him. But he's married now, what can I do? I can't fall in the hole. So that's the point I moved in that direction and the first time we get to go back to New York from Cleveland I meet a boy in Cleveland, he must have been about 13 or 14 years old. I told him when he gets out of school

-- when he gets 15 and gets out of school, I want him to come to New York to be with me, this boy. So when he got out of school, that's the first thing he thought about, coming to me. He did. And I gave him a job as a valet. I needed somebody to valet me, to put on my coat and pants -- no, but I had him to run errands, go to the store and get sandwiches or wipe off the car.
I mean, who was this person?
The person, that boy I told you I found in Cleveland. A boy I met in Cleveland.
Was there something that attracted you to him in particular?
Well, the point of it, I thought he'd be just a nice boy for the job.
No, I wasn't looking for no nothing. It dawned on me that he would be just the one.
